$\begin{aligned} & y \in\left[0, a+e^{|x|}-e^{-x}\right] \\ & \text { (i) If } x \geq 0 \Rightarrow y \in\left(0, a+e^x-\frac{1}{e^x}\right) \\ & \text { if } x \lt 0 \Rightarrow y \in\left(0, a+e^{-x}-e^{-x}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow y \in(0, a)\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Area }=(a)+\int_0^1\left(a+e^x-e^{-x}\right) d x=\frac{e^2+8 e+1}{e} \\ & =a+\left.\left(a x+e^x+e^{-x}\right)\right|_0 ^1=e+8+\frac{1}{e} \\ & =a+\left(a+e+\frac{1}{e}-2\right)=e+\frac{1}{e}+8 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 a-2=8 \Rightarrow a=5\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The area enclosed by the closed curve $C$ given by the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{x + a}{y - 2} = 0, y\left(1\right) = 0$~is $4\pi$.~Let $P$ and $Q$ be the points of intersection of the curve $C$ and the $y$-axis. If normals at $P$ and $Q$ on the curve $C$ intersect $x$-axis at points $R$ and $S$ respectively, then the length of the line segment $RS$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{x + a}{y - 2} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x + a}{2 - y}$

$⇒ \left(2 - y\right)dy = \left(x + a\right)dx$

$⇒ 2y - \dfrac{y2}{2} = \dfrac{x2}{2} + ax + c$

Put~$x = 1$, then we get~$y\left(1\right) = 0$.

$a + c = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now,

$4y - y^{2} = x^{2} + 2ax + 2c$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + 2ax - 4y + 2c = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} + 2ax - 4y - 1 - 2a = 0$

This is a circle having radius

$r = \sqrt{a^{2} + 4 + 1 + 2a} = \sqrt{\left(a + 1\right)2 + 4}$

Now,

$\pir^{2} = 4\pi$

$r^{2} = 4$

$⇒ \sqrt{\left(a + 1\right)2 + 4} = 4$

$⇒ \left(a + 1\right)2 = 0$

So,~$a = - 1$

Hence, circle is

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 4y + 1 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)2 + \left($y - 2\right)2 = 4$

It cuts~$y$-axis~at~$x = 0$, so

$P ≡ \left(0, 2 + \sqrt{3}\right) \text{ and } Q ≡ \left($0, 2 - $\sqrt{3}\right)

Now,

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 4y + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2x + $2y\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) -$2 - $4\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) =$0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = \dfrac{1 - x}{y - 2}

$⇒ - \left(\dfrac{dx}{dy}\right) = \dfrac{y - 2}{x - 1}

Slope of normal at~$P$~is

${m}_{1} = $\dfrac{2 + \sqrt{3} - 2}{0 - 1} = - \sqrt{3}

Slope of normal at~$Q$~is

${m}_{2} = $\dfrac{2 - \sqrt{3} - 2}{0 - 1} = \sqrt{3}

Equation of normal at $Q$~is

$y - \left($2 - $\sqrt{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}\left(x - 0\right)$

$⇒ y - \left(2 - \sqrt{3}\right) = \sqrt{3}x$

Equation of normal at~$P$~is

$y - 2 - \sqrt{3} = - \sqrt{3} \left(x - 0\right)$

$⇒ y = - $\sqrt{3}$x + 2 + $\sqrt{3}

So,

$R ≡ \left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3},0\right)$~and~$S ≡ \left(1 - $\dfrac{2}{3},$0\right)$

Hence,

$RS = \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3}}{3}$& units

$⇒ - x^{2} + 2x + 8 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} - 2x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 4\right)\left(x + 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = 4, - 2$

So, the required area is given by,

$A = \mathop{∫}_{- 2}^{4}\left(\left(6 - x\right) - \left(\dfrac{16}{x + 4}\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ A = {6x - \dfrac{x2}{2} - 16\log \left|x + 4\right|}_{- 2}^{4}$

$⇒ A = \left(24 - 8 - 16\log \left|$8\right|\right) - \left(-$12 - 2 - 16\log 2\right)$

$⇒ A = 16 - $16\log \left|$8\right| + 14 + 16\log 2$

$⇒ A = 30 - 32\ln 2

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Plotting the diagram of given data we have,

Now finding limit by diagram, we get

$x\dfrac{2}{3} + x\dfrac{2}{3} = 1$

$⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$

So total area will be given by,

$A = {∫}_{- \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}}^{0}\left(1 - x\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\dfrac{3}{2} d x - \left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \times \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right) + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(1 - x\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}dx$

Now for solving~$∫ \left(1 - x\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}dx$

~Let~$x = \sin^{3}\theta$

$= ∫ \left(1 - \sin^{2}\theta\right)\dfrac{3}{2} \cdot 3\sin^{2}\theta cos\thetad\theta$

$= ∫ 3\sin^{2}\theta\cos^{4}\thetad\theta$

$= 3 ∫ \sin^{2}\theta\cos^{4}\thetad\theta$

Now putting the limit and solving we get

$⇒ A = \dfrac{9\pi}{64} - \dfrac{1}{16} + \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{36\pi}{256}$

$⇒ \dfrac{256A}{π} = 36$
